bracket: [Misprint in the stem, preserved as printed. Two things are wrong with it: 'susceptibility of magnetism' should read 'of magnesium' (magnetism is a phenomenon, not a substance), and \(1.2 \times 10^{-15}\) should be \(1.2 \times 10^{-5}\) - a real paramagnetic susceptibility is of order \(10^{-5}\). The chapter settles it internally: the March 2016 question in this same chapter runs the identical problem backwards for magnesium, with \(\chi = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\) at 200 K falling to \(1.2 \times 10^{-5}\) at 300 K. Nothing in the working changes - the answer depends only on the ratio \(T_{1}/T_{2}\), so only the power of ten moves.]
